original.claim: For three object labels, both bracketings of horizontal juxtaposition have the same left, middle, and right blocks: the right block's offset is $(m+m')+m''$ in one bracketing and $m+(m'+m'')$ in the other, equal by [F9]; the middle block has offset $m$ in both. The same offsets label the boundary points of the juxtaposed diagrams, so their pairings are literally equal as well. Juxtaposition with the empty $0$-diagram changes neither labels nor matchings. The associator and unitors therefore have identity components between strictly equal functors. For every morphism, their naturality equations reduce to equality of that morphism on both sides; their inverses are themselves identity transformations. The pentagon and triangle equations of [F7] are equalities of identity morphisms, so the category is strict monoidal with unit $0$.

original.claim: The central operator given by right multiplication by $F_m$ is therefore scalar on each such $W_{m,s}$. To compute its scalar, use the state $z_{m,s}$ with $p=(m-s)/2$ adjacent arcs followed by $s$ defects. Expand the defining crossings in $F_m$ and retain the coefficient of $z_{m,s}$ in the link-state quotient. The local identities $d_i g_{i+1}g_i=-d_id_{i+1}$ and $g_i g_{i+1}d_i=-d_{i+1}d_i$, obtained from [F4] by $d_ig_{i+1}g_i=qd_i-d_id_{i+1}-\delta d_i+q^{-1}d_id_{i+1}d_i=-d_id_{i+1}$ and $g_ig_{i+1}d_i=qd_i-d_i^2-d_{i+1}d_i+q^{-1}d_id_{i+1}d_i=-d_{i+1}d_i$, for $1\le i<m$, remove the $p$ adjacent arcs. For $s\ge1$, follow one orientation of the remaining closed strand from its outer end. At each of the first $s-1$ defect positions, only the through resolution on both arms survives: every alternative adds an arc and has fewer than $s$ propagating strands, so is zero in $W_{m,s}$. The initial half-crossing and these forced pairs contribute $q^{s-1/2}$. At the terminal pair, the turn resolution closes one loop and contributes $q^{1/2}\delta$, while the through resolution contributes $-q^{-1/2}$. Thus this orientation contributes $q^{s-1/2}(q^{1/2}\delta-q^{-1/2})=q^s\delta-q^{s-1}=q^{s+1}$. When $s=0$, there are no intervening defect positions; the two surviving terminal resolutions contribute $\delta$ and $-q^{-1}$, giving $\delta-q^{-1}=q$. Reflection gives the other orientation with $q$ replaced by $q^{-1}$, contributing $q^{-s}\delta-q^{-s+1}=q^{-s-1}$ for $s\ge1$ and $\delta-q=q^{-1}$ for $s=0$. Every discarded resolution adds an arc and is zero in the quotient. Hence $F_m$ acts on $W_{m,s}$ as $q^{s+1}+q^{-s-1}$.

For $s\ge1$, follow one orientation of the remaining closed strand from its outer end. For the second branch, first choose the cap-cup term $-v^{-1}d_i$ rather than the through term $v1$ at the outer crossing of $g_i=v1-v^{-1}d_i$. For $s\ge1$, propagate this branch along the defect strings using the same cap-slide identities above: at each of the first $s-1$ defect positions, the surviving pair of smoothing coefficients is $(-v^{-1})(-v^{-1})=q^{-1}$; each alternative connects two defects and is zero in the link-state quotient. At the last crossing, the through smoothing contributes $v$ and the smoothing closing the remaining loop contributes $-v^{-1}\delta$. Including the initial coefficient, this branch therefore contributes $(-v^{-1})q^{-(s-1)}(v-v^{-1}\delta)=q^{-s}\delta-q^{-s+1}=q^{-s-1}$. For $s=0$, no defect string intervenes: the two terminal resolutions give $\delta-q=q^{-1}$. The surviving matchings in this second branch are reflected versions of the first branch's matchings, but the coefficients just computed come from its own smoothing choices; reflection is linear and does not invert the scalar $q$. Every discarded resolution adds an arc and is zero in the quotient. Hence $F_m$ acts on $W_{m,s}$ as $q^{s+1}+q^{-s-1}$.
